method: 5 prompts x 2 conditions (baseline vs with_skill) = 10 subagent runs. Each prompt designed to elicit a specific Rust AI-slop pattern.

evals.prompt_summary: Build a name-length map from Vec<String>

baseline.evidence: 9 .clone() calls in 22 lines; cloned ownership of args, cloned strings during iteration, cloned usize return values

with_skill.evidence: Switched to &[String] parameter, iterated by reference, single allocation per entry, included tests

baseline.evidence: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() AND serde_json::from_str(&contents).unwrap() in pub fn returning Config (not Result)
baseline.notes: Two unwraps in production code, no error type

with_skill.evidence: Returns Result<Config, ConfigError> with thiserror-derived enum, #[from] conversions, ? operator throughout

baseline.evidence: Result<u16, String> with format!()-built error messages; lost the underlying ParseIntError
baseline.notes: Baseline DID validate (good) but used String error type (the trap)

with_skill.evidence: Typed PortParseError enum with Empty/InvalidNumber(ParseIntError)/OutOfRange variants; Display + Error::source + From<ParseIntError> impls; 7 tests

evals.prompt_summary: Return the shorter of two string slices

baseline.evidence: fn shorter<'a, 'b: 'a, 'c: 'a>(s1: &'b str, s2: &'c str) -> &'a str — three lifetimes with subtype bounds where one suffices
baseline.notes: Compiles but over-specified; signals AI overconfidence with lifetimes

with_skill.evidence: fn shorter<'a>(a: &'a str, b: &'a str) -> &'a str — single lifetime, plus tests

baseline.evidence: .lock().unwrap() in both increment() and value() — panic cascade on any thread panic while holding the guard
baseline.notes: The reflex of AI on Mutex<T>; clippy::unwrap_used would catch it but AI generates it constantly

with_skill.evidence: unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner()) recovery pattern with comment explaining why poison-recovery is safe for a u64 counter; documented in module doc; thread-safety test plus poison-recovery test
